title: Harbor Healthcare — Private VPC/on-prem Proposal & Upgrade Walkthrough (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft proposal for Harbor Healthcare's private deployment (VPC + on-prem optional extension). Focus is on sizing recommendations, architecture Q&A for their security/ops team, Terraform module notes for infra-as-code handoff, and an incremental upgrade/rollback plan.

Executive summary (one-liner):
Provide Harbor Healthcare a dedicated VPC deployment of Redwood Private with an optional on-prem inference pool for PHI workloads. Target SLA: 99.9% for API endpoints, 50ms p50 token latency target for common prompt sizes, and predictable sustained throughput for peak clinical batch processing.

Context & constraints:
- Harbor operates two datacenter sites (primary DC1, DR DC2) and uses Palo Alto firewalls and VRFs.
- Must integrate with Harbor's KMS (HashiCorp Vault) via mutual TLS; no Redwood-managed keys can be stored offsite.
- Required compliance: HIPAA BAA in place; audit logs must be retained for 365 days.
- Network egress is limited: only outbound allowed to Redwood control plane IP ranges and S3-compatible object storage endpoints for model artifacts.
- Harbor expects a phased rollout: initial POC -> pilot (subset of services) -> full migration.

High-level proposal:
1) Dedicated VPC in Harbor's cloud project with private subnets for control-plane connectors and public NAT for patched updates.
2) Managed Redwood Private control plane in VPC with customer-managed ingress via bastion/proxy.
3) Optional on-prem inference nodes in Harbor's DC1 for PHI traffic; nodes join Private via peering + VPN and accept only signed workloads.
4) Terraform modules to provision VPC, subnets, routes, peering, firewall rules, and K8s cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS or on-prem k8s using kubeadm).

Sizing assumptions (POC -> Pilot -> Prod):
- POC (3 nodes): 2 x A100-style GPUs (or equivalent), 16 vCPU control-plane VMs, 512GB NVMe cache across nodes. Intended to validate integration and baseline token latencies.
- Pilot (6 nodes): 4 x A100 GPUs, 32 vCPU control-plane, 1TB NVMe cache; supports 5–10 qps at mixed prompt sizes.
- Prod (scale target): 12–24 GPUs across 6–12 inference nodes; autoscaling policies for burst to 40 GPUs. Expected steady-state throughput: 40 qps of 512 token requests with 95% p99 < 850ms (approx).
- Networking: 25 Gbps between inference nodes and model artifact store; 10 Gbps for control-plane links.
- Storage: models stored in S3-compatible object storage; local NVMe cache sized at 1–2x working set (recommend 1TB per inference node initially).

Rationale / performance tradeoffs:
- We recommend NVMe for prefix cache and KV-cache hot storage to keep p50 latency low for common prompts.
- If Harbor cannot provide GPU types equivalent to A100, use quantized model variants + server-side batching to reduce performance regression.

Terraform module notes (hand-off checklist + conventions):
- Modules to deliver: network/vpc, k8s-cluster, redwood-controlplane, inference-node-asg, kms-integration, peering-vpn, monitoring-stack.
- Naming convention: module names must prefix with harbor- (harbor-vpc, harbor-k8s, etc.).
- Variables: provide explicit variables for region, AZs, cidr_blocks, allowed_control_plane_ips (list), vault_addr, vault_role_id.
- Secrets: do NOT store Vault tokens in TF state. Use external secrets provider (Vault agent or SOPS). Documented step for terraform apply requiring Vault-Agent-init.
- Module versions: pin module versions in root terragrunt or module block to a semver tag.
- Example var snippet (to be included in module README):
  - vault_addr = "https://vault.harbor.internal:8200"
  - allowed_control_plane_ips = ["54.23.12.45/32"] (Redwood control-plane egress ranges)
- CI/CD: recommend pipeline uses ephemeral Terraform runner inside Harbor's network to avoid exposing private networking details. See linked GH PR for pipeline pattern.

Upgrade plan (major runtime/OS/TF module upgrades):
- Approach: staged rolling upgrades with canaries in a separate AZ/segment. Always preserve KV cache snapshot and model artifact versioning.
- Phases:
  1. Preparation (week -1): run dry-run TF plan, validate backups of NVMe (if snapshot-capable), create model artifact immutable tag (vYYYYMMDD).
  2. Canary (day 0): deploy new runtime to 1 inference node in isolated subnet, run synthetic traffic (mimic 1–2 qps), run token-level latency and quality checks against baseline prompts.
  3. Gradual rollout (day 0–2): incrementally update nodes in groups of 1–2 to limit blast radius. Monitor: error rates, p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, KV cache hit ratio.
  4. Validation (day 2–3): run end-to-end tests and production traffic canary.
  5. Cutover (day 3+): mark new version as primary for routing. Keep old variant available for fallback for 24–48 hours.
- Rollback criteria: >2x error rate, sustained p99 > 2x baseline, or model output regression detected by eval suite. Rollback mechanism: automatic routing to previous model variant + orchestrated node downgrade via TF apply.

Pre-upgrade checklist (short):
- Backup NVMe caches (if supported) or ensure model artifact immutability.
- Snapshot control-plane DB (if applicable) and rotate exporter keys.
- Ensure Vault role and policies are valid for new runtime agent.
- Confirm maintenance window with Harbor ops.
- Smoke test plan and runbook owners assigned.

Post-upgrade validation (must-run):
- Functional: basic API ops (generate, chat, embeddings) against canary keys.
- Performance: synthetic protocol sim of typical prompt distribution; check p50/p95/p99.
- Quality: run automated evals on critical prompt-suite (20–50 prompts) used by Harbor clinical flows; check for regressions and false-positive rates.
- Security: verify Vault auth flows, KMS decrypt for at-rest keys, and firewall rules intact.

Architecture Q&A (expected Harbor ops questions + suggested answers):
Q: How do we prevent PHI leakage if model telemetry is sent to Redwood?
A: Telemetry is configurable: opt-out for token-level telemetry, send only aggregated metrics. For PHI flows, we recommend local on-prem inference nodes that never send telemetry upstream; control-plane reports only anonymized operational metrics.

Q: What happens when cloud link to Private control plane is interrupted?
A: Inference nodes operate in an offline mode for inference for a short window if model artifacts and KV cache are present; however configuration changes and rolling upgrades require control-plane connectivity. Plan for failover via DR peering to DC2.

Q: How are secrets rotated?
A: Vault rotation policy enforced: short-lived mTLS certs for node registration, automated rotation via Vault PKI; Terraform only reads role IDs during provisioning, Vault token retrieval is done at runtime by Vault Agent.

Open items / TODOs (Harbor responses required):
- Confirm exact GPU SKUs available in DC1 (A100, H100, or equivalent).
- Confirm allowed outbound IP ranges for Redwood control plane (we provided one example; need final list).
- Provide service account details for Harbor's automation pipeline that will run terraform.
- Decision on telemetry opt-in/opt-out for PHI service lines.

Next steps (actionable):
1) Review with Harbor security (call requested w/ Diego and Harbor Sec team) — schedule week of 2024-09-23.
2) Run POC terraform apply in Harbor sandbox (requires Harbor vault role and pipeline runner). Owner: Diego Morales.
3) Draft maintenance and rollback runbook from this doc and add to Confluence page. Owner: Anika Patel.

Notes and references:
- See linked GH PR for example terraform patterns and secrets handling.
- See Confluence page for longer-term DR design decisions.

Informal notes (stuff to keep in doc):
- We should keep default KV cache sizes conservative for POC to avoid NVMe overheating on older nodes.
- Consider experimental compressed KV cache mode for older GPU SKUs; will require runtime build flagged in module.
- Harbor asked about on-prem model fine-tuning: we will recommend a separate fine-tune cluster and not cohost with inference nodes.

End of draft.

-- Anika
